title.en: Haustlong: Thjodolfr's Shield-Lay and the Kenning Myths
title.zh: 《哈勞頌》：希約德爾弗的盾頌與隱喻神話

region.zh: 挪威阿格德爾克維納（詩人故鄉）

texts.period: c. 900 CE (skaldic shield-poem); preserved in Snorri's Skaldskaparmal quotations and MS R (14th c.); text in Corpus Poeticum Boreale (1883)

source.work: Thjodolfr of Hvinir, Haustlong; ed. Vigfusson & Powell, CPB 1883; Skaldic Poetry database

texts.license: Public domain (CPB 1883); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: The oldest narrative skaldic poem: a shield-description in dróttkvætt metre, its panels naming three myth-scenes - Idunn's abduction by the eagle Thjazi, the burning of the eagle and the hostageship of Skadi, and the duel of Thor and Hrungnir with the stone-skull - and its refrains credit the pagan gods as the poem's own audience ('so that? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - 'the? - the record is the myth corpus's oldest dated mythic narrative in verse: the shield as the myth-book of the 10th-century court.
summary.zh: 最古老的敘事吟遊詩：以德羅特克維特律詩寫成的盾面描述，其嵌板命名三個神話場景——伊登被巨鷹夏茲擄走、巨鷹被焚與斯卡蒂的人質身份，以及索爾與赫朗格尼爾的石顱決鬥——並在疊句中將異教諸神視為詩歌的受眾。此記錄是語料中最古老的、可斷代的韻文神話敘事：10世紀宮廷的盾面神話書。

texts.canonical_translation: Corpus Poeticum Boreale, ed. Vigfusson & Powell, Oxford 1883 (public domain); Russell Poole's commentary (Skaldic database)

narrative.en:
Haustlong ('autumn-long') is the myth corpus's oldest dated mythic narrative in verse, and its medium is the shield. The frame: the skald Thjodolfr of Hvinir (c. 900, at the court of Jarl Sigurd of Hladir) describes a shield given him; the shield's paintings are the poem's three panels, and each is a myth told in the tight dróttkvætt metre with its refrains invoking the pagan gods as witnesses ('the? - 'poem's? - 'own? - 'refrain: 'so? - 'that? - 'the? - 'gods? - may? - 'the? - - the skald credits Odin, Thor and the Aesir as the tale's guarantors).

The panels: the Idunn-abduction (the eagle Thjazi carrying off the keeper of the gods' youth - the record norse-idunn-apples holds the Snorri-retelling; the poem is its oldest source); the eagle's burning and Skadi's arrival (the armed giantess at Asgard's gate, the atonement-clause that founds the Njord-marriage - the poem's panel documents the feud-settlement a generation before the prose); and the Thor-Hrungnir duel (the stone-hearted giant, the whetstone shivered, the hammer crushing the skull - the record norse-thor-hrungnir holds the prose; the poem is its skaldic witness).

The record's cultural functions are the shield-poem doctrine (myth as painting-description: the skald's ekphrasis as the myth-book of a court without books) and the kenning-myth doctrine: the kennings that name each figure (the 'keeper of the gods' youth', the 'stone-hearted one', the 'enemy of the? - giants) require the myths as their key - so the poem is simultaneously narrative and dictionary. And its dating is the record's critical datum: c. 900 makes Haustlong the earliest witness for the Idunn, Thjazi and Hrungnir myths, centuries before the Edda-MSS - the court-poetry as the myth corpus's oldest narrative stratum.

In the atlas, the record anchors the shield-poem family: each a tradition's myth-paintings described in verse; the Norse one is distinctive in its metre's discipline and its refrains' theology. For the database, this whole-poem node complements the episode-records it sources: here the shield-lay runs whole.

The metre's discipline completes the record: dróttkvætt's strict internal rhyme and half-line constraints make the shield-lay the myth tradition's most technically demanding verse-form - the myths told inside a prosodic machine, which is why Snorri quoted the poem as his exemplar for teaching the metre. And the skald's biography completes the context: Thjodolfr served the Hladir jarls at the height of the pagan court's power, so the poem's theology (the gods invoked as the tale's guarantors) is the pre-conversion court's own creed - the shield-lay as both myth-book and religious document, dated a generation before the conversion.

Oldest witness datum: c. 900, centuries before the Edda-MSS

title.en: Hrafnagaldur Odins: The Late, Controversial Eddic Poem
title.zh: 《奧丁的烏鴉咒歌》：晚出而有爭議的埃達詩

region.en: The Eddic manuscript-tradition (symbolic pin at Pingvellir, Iceland)
region.zh: 埃達抄本傳統（象徵性定位於冰島辛格韋德利）

texts.period: Preserved in 17th-century paper copies of the Prose Edda tradition; composition date disputed (late medieval or 17th-century)

source.work: Hrafnagaldur Odins (Forspjallsljod); principal MSS: 17th-c. copies in the Prose Edda tradition; study: Kristjan Arnason & Thorunn Sigurdardottir, 2011

texts.license: Public domain (early editions); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: The myth corpus's most controversial poem: a mythological lay (once printed as 'Forspjallsljod', 'the prelude-lay') preserved only in late copies, narrating Idunn's fall from the ash, the goddesses' journey to consult Odin and the norns, and a prophecy of the world's dimming - the twilight before Ragnarok, with the gods suffering and asking the norns' judgment. Its authenticity is the record's subject: scholars have argued it is a late medieval or even 17th-century composition (the philologists' verdict), while its defenders read it as a genuine late-eddic lay - the poem as a case-study in myth-detection.
summary.zh: 神話語料中最具爭議的詩篇：一首神話頌歌（曾被刊為「序詩」Forspjallsljod），僅存於晚期抄本，敘述伊登自梣樹跌落、眾女神前去求問奧丁與命運三女神，以及世界趨暗——諸神黃昏前的薄暮——的預言，其中諸神受苦並求問女神之裁決。其真偽正是此記錄的主題：語文學者多斷其為中世紀晚期甚至17世紀之作，而辯護者則讀其為真正的晚期埃達詩——這首詩本身就是神話鑑定學的案例研究。

texts.canonical_translation: Hrafnagaldur Odins ed. in Kristjan Arnason & Thorunn Sigurdardottir, Hrafnagaldur Odins, 2011; older editions public domain

narrative.en:
Hrafnagaldur Odins ('Odin's raven-galdr') is the myth corpus's authentication-problem in verse, and its content is a twilight-prophecy. The narrative: Idunn falls from Yggdrasil's branches (the keeper of the gods' youth struck down 'in? - the? - 'midst? - of? - 'the? - 'ash? - the twilight's first casualty); the goddesses ride to Odin and to the norns to ask the meaning; the norns answer with the world's dimming - the gods' sufferings beginning, 'the? - 'gods? - 'under? - 'the? - 'cloud? - 'of? - 'sorrow? - the prophecy of the age before Ragnarok, and the poem's frames ('the? - 'raven? - 'sings? - 'the? - galdr? - 'of? - Odin) give the title.

The authenticity-problem is the record's real subject: the poem survives only in 17th-century paper copies appended to the Prose Edda tradition (no medieval witness); its metre is archaic and its myth-content consistent with the Edda, but the philologists' verdict (Sophus Bugge and the editorial tradition) has been that it is a late composition - possibly 17th-century, possibly an antiquarian forgery in eddic style - while the 2011 linguistic study (Kristjan Arnason and Thorunn Sigurdardottir) argued for genuine late-medieval composition on grammatical grounds. The dispute is the record's lesson: the myth corpus's authentication is a live philological method, and this poem is its test-case.

The record's cultural functions are the reception-doctrine (the poem's history: printed in early editions of the Poetic Edda, dismissed, re-argued - the myth corpus's editorial afterlife) and the twilight-prophecy doctrine (the narrative's own frame: the age before the doom, the gods suffering and asking the norns - the eschatology's mood-painting). In the atlas, the record anchors the contested-authenticity family: each a tradition's disputed document; the Hrafnagaldur one is distinctive in being printed as canonical and then demoted - the database's own method (provenance, manuscript-witness, linguistic dating) documented on a poem.

For the database, this node documents the corpus's limits: a mythic narrative whose truth-value is a scholarly dispute - the record preserves it with its status labeled.

The poem's content-completeness documents why the dispute matters: the lay names the twilight's cast (Idunn's fall, the goddesses' ride, the norns' verdict, the gods' sufferings under the cloud) in language consistent with the Edda-tradition, so an authentic date would add a genuine late-eddic eschatology to the corpus - and a late date would instead document the 17th century's antiquarian myth-making. The record thus holds both readings, with the poem's status labeled: the myth corpus's own authentication-method (manuscript-witness, metre, grammar) applied to its most disputed text.

title.en: Voluspa Complete: The Sibyl's Vision from the Void to the Renewal
title.zh: 《女先知的預言》全篇：自鴻蒙至更新的先知幻象

region.en: The sibyl's hall between worlds (symbolic pin at Pingvellir, Iceland)
region.zh: 兩界之間的女先知之廳（象徵性定位於冰島辛格韋德利）

texts.period: c. 900-1000 CE; principal MS Codex Regius GKS 2365 4to (c. 1270s); Hauksbok variant AM 544 4to

source.work: Voluspa (complete poem, st. 1-66); critical ed. Ursula Dronke (Poetic Edda II, 1997)

texts.license: Public domain (Bellows 1923); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: The corpus's master-poem in full: the compelled seeress recites the world's whole biography in sixty-six stanzas - the void, Ymir, the sun and moon, the first humans, the golden age, the first war, Gullveig, the norns, Baldr's death, the genealogy of doom (Loki's brood), the Fimbulwinter, the doom-litany, the battles, the renewal (Baldr's return, Gimle, the last pair), and the dragon flying from the corpse-shore. The poem is the north's prophetic history of the world and the skeleton of all Norse mythography.
summary.zh: 語料的核心長詩全篇：受迫的女先知以六十六節詩句述說世界的完整傳記——鴻蒙、尤彌爾、日月、最初人類、黃金時代、第一場戰爭、古爾維格、命運三女神、巴爾德之死、末日族譜（洛基之群）、芬布爾之冬、末日頌、諸戰、更新（巴爾德歸返、吉姆萊、末世雙親），以及自屍骸之濱飛出的巨龍。此詩是北方的世界預言史，也是所有北歐神話書寫的骨架。

texts.canonical_translation: Henry A. Bellows, The Poetic Edda, New York 1923 (public domain); consulted against Dronke 1997

narrative.en:
Voluspa complete is the myth corpus's master-poem, and this record holds it as one vision. The frame: Odin compels the vala - the dead or trance-bound seeress - to recite before 'the sons of Heimdall' (the frame-record norse-voluspa-sibyl holds the performance); the recitation is the poem's body, and its architecture is the world's biography in six movements. The creation-movements: the void ('there? - 'was? - 'no? - sand? - 'no? - sea? - 'no? - cool? - waves), Ymir and the rime-giants, the sun and moon set on courses, the first humans of Ask and Embla, the golden age and its end (the three giant-maidens with gold), the first war (Gullveig thrice burned, the Vanir's broken oaths).

The fate-movements: the norns at the well ('lawless? - 'they? - 'were? - born? - 'till? - 'three? - came), the deaths of Baldr (the mistletoe, the blind Hodr, Loki's forcing), Loki's brood (the wolf, the serpent, the hag of the iron-wood), the Fimbulwinter and the doom-litany ('an? - axe-age? - 'a? - sword-age? - 'a? - wind-age? - 'a? - wolf-age? - 'till? - 'the? - world? - falls), the battles (Naglfar, the Muspell-riders, Odin-Fenrir, Thor-serpent, the nine paces, Surt's fire). And the renewal-movement: the green earth from the sea, Baldr and Hodr's return, Gimle, the game-pieces found in the grass, Lif and Lifthrasir - and the dragon flying from the corpse-shore, corpses in its feathers, 'and? - 'now? - 'she? - will? - sink.

The record's cultural functions are the master-poem doctrine (the corpus's complete cosmology and eschatology in one vision, the skeleton on which Gylfaginning was built) and the prophecy-genre doctrine (the world's history recited by an unwilling professional woman - myth as a compelled, paid, gendered performance). And the poem's two versions are the record's critical datum: the Codex Regius text (canonical) and the Hauksbok variant (adding the utiseta-frame, the giant-sibyl's title, and other stanzas) - the master-text's own manuscript-history documented. In the atlas, the record anchors the prophetic-history family: each a tradition's whole world-story recited by a seer; the Norse one is distinctive in sixty-six stanzas and an unwilling voice.

For the database, this whole-poem node complements the frame-record and the thematic records it feeds (the creation, war, Baldr, renewal records): here the vision runs whole, void to dragon.

The poem's architecture completes the doctrine: the six movements are symmetric (creation and renewal share the same plain, the same game-pieces, the same sun), so the vision is built as a palindrome of the world's biography - the end written to mirror the beginning. And the seeress's voice completes the genre: the refrain 'do you understand yet, or what?' punctuates the stanzas like an exam-instructor's challenge - prophecy as pedagogy, the audience required to answer, the corpus's own reader-address built into the master-poem.

title.en: Atlakvida: The Lay of Atli and the Niflungs' Last Ride
title.zh: 《阿特利之歌》：阿特利與尼弗隆末代騎行

region.en: Atli's hall on the Danube plain (symbolic pin at Buda, Hungary)
region.zh: 多瑙河平原阿特利大廳（象徵性定位於匈牙利布達）

texts.period: c. 1000-1200 CE; principal MS Codex Regius GKS 2365 4to

source.work: Atlakvida (complete); critical ed. Ursula Dronke (Poetic Edda II, 1997)

texts.license: Public domain (Bellows 1923); passages below are labeled paraphrases

summary.en: The verse lay of the Atli-story: Atli's messenger lures Gunnar and Hogni with the promise of gold; Gudrun's warning-ring carries the wolf's hair; the brothers ride knowing ('gold? - 'they? - 'could? - not? - 'refuse? - the invitation's death-wish built into the gift-economy); Hogni laughs at the heart-test, Gunnar plays the harp with his toes in the snake-pen, Gudrun kills her sons and serves them, and Atli dies in his bed - the lay ending with Gudrun's grief and the halls' burning. The record is the Atli-story's compact verse-telling, companion to the saga-prose.
summary.zh: 阿特利故事的詩體頌歌：阿特利的信使以黃金誘騙吉烏基與霍格尼；古德倫的警示戒指纏有狼毛；兄弟明知有詐仍騎行（「黃金他們無法拒絕」——死亡之願已內嵌於贈禮經濟之中）；霍格尼在心臟測試中大笑，吉烏基在蛇坑中以腳趾彈琴，古德倫殺子設宴，阿特利死於床榻——頌歌以古德倫的悲慟與焚燒的大廳作結。此記錄是阿特利故事的緊湊詩體敘述，與薩迦散文互為補充。

texts.canonical_translation: Henry A. Bellows, The Poetic Edda, New York 1923 (public domain)

narrative.en:
Atlakvida is the Atli-story's compact verse-telling, and its doctrine is the gift-economy's death-logic. The lure: Atli's messenger promises the brothers the Rhine-gold ('rings? - 'and? - 'the? - tribute? - of? - Hun-land? - 'the? - - and the brothers' reply is the poem's most famous clause: they knew the trap and rode - 'gold? - 'they? - 'could? - not? - refuse? - the gift-economy's death-wish stated as ethics: to refuse a lord's summons is cowardice, so the invitation is a death-sentence accepted in gift-currency. Gudrun's warning is the ring with wolf's hair wound in it - the coded signal - and the messenger lies.

The test-scenes: the heart-demand (the thrall's trembling heart exposed as false, Hogni laughing while they cut - 'the? - 'brave? - 'heart? - 'beat? - 'little? - 'when? - 'laid? - 'on? - 'the? - 'hand), the snake-pen and Gunnar's harp (the toes striking the strings, the serpents lulled, one adder striking - the harp's last note), and Gudrun's vengeance (the sons' hearts served at the feast, the bed-kill, the burning). The lay's closing is the corpus's grief-clause: Gudrun's answer to the sea ('the? - 'waves? - 'bore? - me? - 'to? - 'another? - shore? - - the vengeance-cycle's continuation, and the poem's final doctrine: 'so? - 'shall? - 'a? - 'sister? - 'mourn? - 'her? - brothers? - 'the? - record's? - ethic of kin-grief as the fate's own register.

The record's cultural functions are the gift-economy's death-logic doctrine (the invitation as sentence, acceptance as honor) and the compact-verse doctrine: the lay is the corpus's shortest complete heroic narrative (thirty-nine stanzas), the saga's story told in a tenth of the prose - the eddic economy of narrative. And its relation to the Atli-prose (Volsunga chs. 39-44) and to the Greenland lay Atlamal (the dialogue-version) is the record's comparative datum: one story, three tellings, the corpus's transmission documented. In the atlas, the record anchors the vengeance-lay family: each a tradition's kin-feud in verse; the Norse one is distinctive in the harp's toes and the served hearts.

For the database, this whole-poem node complements the Gudrun-Atli record (which synthesizes the prose): here the lay runs whole.

The lay's Attila-kernel completes the record: Atli is the tradition's memory of the Hunnish king (Attila, d. 453, died in his bed - the saga's bed-kill as the historical king's death re-read as vengeance), so the lay documents the migration-age's memory in heroic verse - the north's oldest historical trauma converted to myth. And the grief-clause completes the doctrine: the closing counsel ('so shall a sister mourn her brothers') makes the vengeance-cycle's cost its own ethic - the corpus's most compact statement that victory and mourning are one payment.

title.en: Sigrdrifumal: The Valkyrie's Wisdom-Lay in Full
title.zh: 《勝利授予者之歌》：女武神智慧頌全篇

region.en: Hindarfjall's fire-girt hall (symbolic pin at Rhine valley)
region.zh: 欣達山火焰環繞之廳（象徵性定位於萊茵河谷）

source.work: Sigrdrifumal (complete); critical ed. Ursula Dronke (Poetic Edda II, 1997)

summary.en: The valkyrie's curriculum in full: the waking (Sigurd cutting the byrnie), the memory-beer with its blessing formula (the bragarfull rite in detail), the great rune-catalog with its cutting-surfaces (shield, bark, grain-ear, glass, gold, wolf's claw, bear's paw, ice, serpent's eggs), the speech-runes and ale-runes, and the wisdom-teaching - conduct, ale-craft, and the counsel against speech-evil. The record is the corpus's most complete magic-and-conduct textbook, delivered by a punished chooser of the slain.
summary.zh: 女武神的全部課程：甦醒（西格魯德割開甲胄）、附有祝聖套語的記憶之酒（詳載「祝杯」儀式）、附有刻寫載體清單的如尼大目錄（盾、樹皮、穀穗、玻璃、黃金、狼爪、熊掌、冰、蛇卵）、言語之符與啤酒之符，以及行為、飲酒之道與慎言的智慧教誨。此記錄是語料中最完整的魔法與行為教科書，由一位受罰的「陣亡者揀選者」親授。

texts.canonical_translation: Henry A. Bellows, The Poetic Edda, New York 1923 (public domain)

narrative.en:
Sigrdrifumal is the corpus's magic-and-conduct textbook in full, and this record holds the curriculum whole. The waking and the beer: Sigurd cuts the byrnie from the fire-hill's sleeper; the valkyrie gives the memory-beer (minni-ol) with the blessing-formula in detail - 'the? - 'cup? - 'blessed? - 'in? - 'the? - names? - 'of? - gods? - 'and? - 'of? - 'the? - 'host? - the bragarfull rite (the oath-cup of the sagas) documented here as liturgy. The rune-catalog: 'victory-runes? - 'cut? - 'on? - the? - sword-hilt? - 'and? - 'named? - twice? - 'in? - Tyr's? - name; 'sea-runes? - 'for? - the? - rudder; 'speech-runes? - 'for? - the? - tongue; 'ale-runes? - 'against? - witchcraft? - in? - the? - drink? - 'and? - 'the? - birth-runes? - 'for? - the? - childbed? - 'and? - 'the? - cutting-surfaces: 'on? - shield? - 'and? - 'oak-bark? - 'and? - 'grain-ear? - 'and? - 'glass? - 'and? - gold? - 'and? - 'amulets? - 'on? - the? - wolf's? - claw? - 'and? - the? - bear's? - paw? - 'on? - ice? - 'and? - 'on? - the? - serpent's? - eggs? - the material inventory of runic practice - the corpus's fullest statement of what runes were cut on, and how ('cut? - them? - 'name? - them? - 'think? - them).

The wisdom-teaching: the conduct-counsels (the ale-craft: 'better? - 'not? - to? - ask? - than? - too? - much? - to? - offer; the speech-craft: 'none? - 'shall? - 'so? - evil? - speak? - 'that? - 'he? - 'for? - his? - mother? - grieves), and the poem's closing counsel - the valkyrie's own teaching on oaths, vengeance and love ('her? - 'counsel? - 'of? - 'the? - 'runes? - 'of? - love? - 'and? - the? - oath-motifs). The record's cultural functions are the taught-magic doctrine (the runic curriculum as a valkyrie's pedagogy, its teacher punished for choosing the wrong victory - the irony the record holds) and the ritual-document doctrine: the memory-beer's blessing and the cutting-surfaces are the corpus's most complete description of how runic magic was actually performed.

In the atlas, the record anchors the magic-curriculum family: each a tradition's codified spell-system taught by a master; the Norse one is distinctive in the material inventory. For the database, this whole-poem node complements the waking-record (norse-brynhild-sigrdrifa): here the teaching runs whole, from the beer to the closing counsel.

passages.text: The valkyrie blessed the memory-beer in the names of gods and the host, and taught the runes: victory-runes on the sword-hilt named twice in Tyr's name, sea-runes for the rudder, speech-runes for the tongue, ale-runes against witchcraft. And the cutting-surfaces: shield and oak-bark and grain-ear, glass and gold and amulets, the wolf's claw and the bear's paw, ice and the serpent's eggs - cut them, name them, think them.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Sigrdrifumal st. 5-19 (Bellows 1923); not verbatim. / Paraphrase of Sigrdrifumal st. 15-17 (Bellows 1923); not verbatim.
